claims.text: Cryogenic deformation of the as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy will form nano-twins and stacking faults.
Nano-twins and stacking faults govern the magnetocaloric response of as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Nano-twins and stacking faults govern hysteresis during magnetic-cooling cycles in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Alloy composition influences the formation of nano-twins and stacking faults in the proposed FeMnNiGeSi-type system.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations influence nano-twin and stacking-fault formation in the proposed FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations can alter phase stability, stacking-fault energy, and fcc-hcp interfacial energy.
Cryogenic conditions favor stacking faults and nano-twins through low or negative stacking-fault energy.
Relative to the undeformed as-deposited baseline, cryogenic deformation will enhance the magnetocaloric response.
Relative to the undeformed as-deposited baseline, cryogenic deformation will reduce hysteresis.
The predicted enhancement and hysteresis reduction apply under cryogenic, low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The exact role of longitudinal spin fluctuations in governing magnetocaloric response and hysteresis is not fully understood.
If longitudinal spin fluctuations do not influence nano-twin and stacking-fault formation, the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis will not be enhanced.

contradictions.description: The prediction is reduced hysteresis, whereas the falsification rule describes the expected or absent effect as hysteresis being 'enhanced.' This reverses or obscures the intended direction of the hysteresis outcome.
